prose: An NBC 5 investigation found that AI-powered cameras mounted on Dallas trash trucks have photographed and assigned 'blight scores' to more than 21,000 properties in four months, flagging possible code violations. A city council member and residents are now pushing back, questioning privacy implications and whether camera-driven enforcement could bring fines to lower-income neighbourhoods least able to pay.
highlights: AI cameras on Dallas trash trucks scored 21,000+ properties in four months
System assigns 'blight scores' to detect possible code violations
City councilmember calls for deeper review of camera-driven enforcement
Residents raise privacy concerns and risk of fines in lower-income areas
NBC 5 obtained the city records through an investigation
